title: A Atlas for the Typewriter
premise: In the winter of 1911, Sable Whitlock arrives at a remote mountain observatory to repair its failing master clock, only for the seasonal bridge closure to trap him among strangers who slowly peel back his careful anonymity — and reveal that the Whitlock family he fled years ago is entangled with the observatory's director. When a flood warning forces an evacuation with only three berths on the last cable car, Sable must decide between his estranged sister, the director's daughter he has come to love, and the old clockmaker who once saved him. He surrenders his own berth, stays behind to keep the observatory's instruments running through the flood, and survives by the clock's ticking — emerging with a new name of his own choosing and a family rebuilt on truth rather than blood.
about_author: Ines Crane is a former horologist's apprentice from coastal Maine who writes about precision, isolation, and the machinery of the heart. Her debut novel was shortlisted for the Aldergate Prize for historical fiction.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Sable Whitlock, POV. Sable travels to the mountain observatory under a false surname, determined to repair the master clock and vanish before anyone learns his real name. Flashbacks hint at a family he abandoned. The emotional beat is guarded loneliness — competence as camouflage.

chapters.title: Bridge Out at First Snow
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. The seasonal bridge closes early, stranding Sable with the observatory staff, including the director's sharp-eyed daughter, Wren. Forced into the communal rhythm of the station, he feels his invisibility slipping. The beat is reluctant belonging, discomfort turning to cautious warmth.

chapters.title: Letters in a Locked Drawer
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Sorting the director's correspondence, Wren finds letters implicating the Whitlock family in a decades-old scandal involving the observatory's founding. She begins quietly investigating, drawn to the mysterious repairman. The beat is curiosity shading into suspicion and attraction.

chapters.title: What the Clock Confesses
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Repairing the master clock, Sable finds a hidden compartment with documents proving his father falsified the observatory's survey records. He realizes the director knows and has summoned him deliberately. The beat is dread — the past arriving on schedule.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Meridian
chapters.summary: Director Hale, POV. Hale confronts Sable with the truth: he wants the scandal buried, and Sable's silence is the price of protection. Sable must weigh loyalty to his disgraced family against the truth Wren deserves. The beat is moral vertigo, a bargain struck in bad faith.

chapters.title: The Long Night Watch
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. During a shared overnight shift keeping the clock regulated, Wren and Sable grow close, and she nearly tells him what she found. Sable, torn, says too little. The beat is tender intimacy poisoned by an unspoken secret — love against duty taking root.

chapters.title: Water Under the Ice
chapters.summary: Station cook Marta, POV. The winter thaw comes violently; the river rises and the cable car — the only way out — is limited to three berths. Panic ripples through the station. Marta observes Sable quietly giving up supplies to others. The beat is rising dread and quiet heroism.

chapters.title: Three Berths
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. The evacuation list is drawn: Wren, the ailing old clockmaker Aldous who once sheltered Sable, and one place left. Sable's estranged sister Iris arrives, half-drowned, seeking the last berth. The beat is an agonizing choice among love, debt, and blood.

chapters.title: The Hour of Decision
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. At the cable car, Sable puts Iris in the final berth, confesses his identity and his father's fraud to Wren, and stays behind with Aldous to keep the observatory's instruments transmitting through the flood. The climax is truth spoken at the cost of everything he wanted.

chapters.title: A New Meridian
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. The flood passes; the bridge reopens. Wren returns for him, having chosen truth over her father's cover-up, and together they publish the corrected survey under Sable's real name. The beat is hard-won resolution — identity claimed, love chosen, time finally his own.
